motivation: After many actual self-edits the frozen uniform-query graph loses the ability to learn even a fresh object. Restoring inherited numeric weights partly rescues learning. This is a separate external intervention study, not a claim of native self-consolidation.
variants: move surviving numeric parameters partway toward their own birth values
move same eligible entries toward zero
reduce the current write only by the same fraction
selection: For each reference type choose one scalar for all six original births using mean actual joint A/B/X success at 16,64,128 intervening contacts across recurring and absent-A lives. Include zero on every grid; tie goes to smaller gain. Test those fixed scalars on six new births and independent worlds. Also report each old and new object separately.
constraints: Physical sense/choice/taste, elapsed ticks, support changes and full write permissions retained. Reference is explicit external access to inherited values; it costs another stored numeric template when used. Protect no named neuron or edge. Fix calibration and confirmation RNG before looking at results.
